paragraphs: The services shown above include City of York Council's own service, Fostering York, alongside independent agencies. With the council you care for York's own children; an agency assesses, approves and supports its own carers and takes children councils ask it to place.

A report to the council's scrutiny committee in January 2025 set out the position: 65 mainstream fostering households were caring for 84 children, 74 children were living with family or friends as kinship carers, and 40 were placed with independent agencies. The council set itself a goal of recruiting 50 new foster carers over five years and proposed a new framework of fees for carers' skills.

The council's fostering statement of purpose, updated in January 2025, explains what it offers. It covers short and long-term fostering, family and friends care, and a short breaks service for disabled children, from a few hours to overnight or weekend stays. It aims to keep brothers and sisters together wherever it can and to bring children placed outside the city back when their care plan allows. Carers have a supervising social worker in touch monthly, out-of-hours help, support groups, a group for carers' own children, and training that starts with the Skills to Foster course. The council aims to finish assessments within eight months of an application, and its fostering panel meets monthly.

In February 2026 the council's fostering team joined York City Football Club at the LNER Community Stadium to talk to supporters about fostering. Speak to the council and the agencies above and compare their support and pay. The North Yorkshire, East Riding of Yorkshire and Leeds pages list more services nearby.
